builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted model uses more compute or memory than your workload can justify.
builder_plan.change: Check for a usable pruned checkpoint and runtime support before attempting model surgery.
builder_plan.baseline: The original unpruned model at the same precision, context, and load.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task quality, actual GPU memory, serving throughput, and preparation cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Learning to Be Truncated: Preparing LLM Checkpoints for SVD Compression
summary: LLift replaces per-compression-ratio recovery fine-tuning after SVD compression with a single distillation-based preparation fine-tune whose updates are merged into the original weights, after which one SVD decomposition is reused across truncation ranks. It costs one fine-tuning run at a single ratio with the original model as teacher (activation and optimizer memory for the target matrices, feasible for a 7B model on constrained hardware only with parameter-efficient setups), plus the cost of validating each downstream budget. It can fail if the claimed cross-ratio transfer does not hold for the reader's model family, task distribution, or compression operator, and SVD-compressed models may still underperform simpler alternatives such as quantization or a natively smaller model.
rationale: If the reader deploys SVD-compressed models at multiple rank budgets, one preparation run replaces repeated per-ratio recovery fine-tuning, but the absolute quality of SVD compression versus quantization or smaller native models must be validated on their workload.
technique: One-shot checkpoint preparation for multi-ratio SVD compression

claims.statement: LLift replaces per-compression-ratio recovery fine-tuning after SVD compression with a single distillation-based preparation fine-tune whose updates are merged into the original weights, after which one SVD decomposition is reused across truncation ranks. It costs one fine-tuning run at a single ratio with the original model as teacher (activation and optimizer memory for the target matrices, feasible for a 7B model on constrained hardware only with parameter-efficient setups), plus the cost of validating each downstream budget. It can fail if the claimed cross-ratio transfer does not hold for the reader's model family, task distribution, or compression operator, and SVD-compressed models may still underperform simpler alternatives such as quantization or a natively smaller model.

Accuracy gains across three SVD compression ratios on LLaMA-7B from a single prepared checkpoint, with no per-ratio fine-tuning; gains reported to extend across model families, sizes, and SVD operators, but no multiplicative factor is stated.
